newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech coalition wins majority of senate seats.
newsitem.headline: Czech coalition wins majority of senate seats.

text.p: The ruling Czech centre-right coalition won a majority of seats in the newly-created upper house of parliament, the Senate, in second round runoff elections on Saturday.

With 60 constituencies out a total of 81 declared, the three parties in the coalition had a total of 41 seats, while opposition parties had 19 seats, according to official results and the Czech news agency CTK.

At 5.35 p.m. (1635 GMT) the senior coalition partner, Civic Democratic Party, had won 25 of the seats declared. Its allies the Christian Democratic Union had 10 seats and the Civic Democratic Alliance six.
The strongest opposition party, the Social Democrats had won 17 seats, with the Communists taking one and an independent candidate winning one seat.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's Civic Democratic Party won three seats outright in last weekend's first round, and 76 candidates qualified for the runoffs.
The Senate is a mostly advisory body with limited legislative powers but the election is the first test at the polls since the coalition lost its majority in the lower house in June.
Turnout was low, with just over 30 percent of the electorate voting out of the districts declared on Saturday.
